    <item>
      <title>European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans</link>
      <description><p>Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans</p><p>The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.</p><p>The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/17/egypt-eu-deal-refugees-mediterranean">promised by Ursula von der Leyen</a>, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/european-commission">European Commission</category>

      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/876babd774d84ecb98a5ee0e9eba98b14d862c89/1434_394_2316_1853/master/2316.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=779e036d6f4f59b8c0421e3491fdb9bb">

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/18/byron-bay-doula-left-newborn-to-inflate-jumping-castle-freebirth-inquest-ntwnfb</link>
      <description><p>Inquest into deaths of four babies born in free births or at home in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 hears ‘something was seriously wrong’</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Baby DH was born in an inflatable pool, in a candle-lit room in his parents’ home near Byron Bay, with no one medically trained present. There are two very different versions of what happened next.</p><p>In the parents’ version, the doula reassured them Baby DH was OK, then left to inflate a jumping castle while their newborn turned purple, became floppy, and struggled to breathe.       <title>How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/how-ukraine-struck-kerch-bridge-symbol-vladimir-putin-rule</link>
      <description><p>With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea</p><p>At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.</p><p>Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/ng-interactive/2026/aug/02/this-is-where-democracy-beats-totalitarianism-ukraines-drone-strike-force-takes-the-fight-to-russia">the work had become almost mundane:</a> they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/how-ukraine-struck-kerch-bridge-symbol-vladimir-putin-rule">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/kessler-twins-assisted-dying-decision</link>
      <description><p>Pop-singing sisters, who died aged 89 last year, described their declining health and desire to depart life together</p><p>Alice and Ellen Kessler, the identical pop-singing twins who chose to jointly end their lives through assisted dying last year, said they had “reached rock bottom” due to health problems and had been relieved to be able to die together.</p><p>The German sisters, who became huge television stars in the 1960s and 70s, especially in Italy and the US, said a catalogue of health conditions had left them with no desire to carry on living.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/kessler-twins-assisted-dying-decision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘They were keeping it for a rainy day’: Ukraine’s Kerch bridge attack is proof Kyiv still has cards to play</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ukraine-kerch-bridge-attack-russia-crimea-analysis</link>
      <description><p>Partial demolition of bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea is obvious embarrassment to Putin days before meeting with Xi and Trump</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/17/europe-ukraine-russia-crimea-kerch-bridge-attack-latest-news-updates">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Ukraine’s attack on the Kerch road bridge overnight is the culmination of weeks, and perhaps months, of military operations plus years of industrial development, during which Kyiv has developed its own cruise missiles and long-range drones.</p><p>The demolition is not quite total, because the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ukraine-strikes-critical-damage-russia-kerch-bridge-crimea">rail bridge is still standing</a>, one line in operation – but the attack is an obvious embarrassment to Russia two days before Vladimir <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/xi-jinping-donald-trump-vladimir-putin-world-peace-trilateral-says-china">Putin is due to meet Donald Trump and Xi Jinping</a> in Shenzhen.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ukraine-kerch-bridge-attack-russia-crimea-analysis">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/nvidia-third-quarter-revenue-jensen-huang</link>
      <description><p>Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy</p><p>Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster.</p><p>Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago. The third-quarter earnings report comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">ouster of Huang</a> over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with his own employees.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/nvidia-third-quarter-revenue-jensen-huang">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Judge extends deadline for Trump’s deposition in $10bn BBC lawsuit</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/17/trump-bbc-deposition-delay</link>
      <description><p>President, who had agreed to sit for deposition in October but backed out, must now appear by 22 January</p><p>Donald Trump has been granted a temporary delay before he must give a witness statement in his $10bn defamation lawsuit against the BBC.</p><p>In late October, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/22/trump-bbc-lawsuit-deposition-discovery">Enjoliqué Lett, a federal magistrate judge, gave Trump a firm 11 December deadline</a> to sit for a deposition by lawyers representing the BBC in his lawsuit against the British broadcaster. If he failed to do so by that date, he could be subject to penalties up to dismissal of the case, the judge warned.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/17/trump-bbc-deposition-delay">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Deutsche Bank dismissed warnings about dealings with risky clients, reports claim</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim</link>
      <description><p>International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits</p><p>Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.</p><p>A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/apr/17/deutsche-bank-faces-action-over-20bn-russian-money-laundering-scheme">been caught being used to launder billions of dollars</a> for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/megaspeed-company-breaks-slience-nvidia-jensen-huang-alice-huang</link>
      <description><p>Company insists Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese spy, left business in late 2025</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/elon-musk-tech-execs-open-letter-jensen-huang-return-nvidia-ceo">Elon Musk joins 165,000 others calling for Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/16/ai-sell-off-resumes-jensen-huang-discusses-comeback-nvidia-ceo-dollar-stock-markets-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Megaspeed International, the company linked to the downfall of the Nvidia chief, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/jensen-huang">Jensen Huang</a>, says it is a “legitimate and lawful business” and has announced that its director, who allegedly had an affair with Jensen Huang, left the business in late 2025.</p><p>The Singapore-based cloud computing company on the weekend said it was “aware of recent media reports containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/megaspeed-company-breaks-slience-nvidia-jensen-huang-alice-huang">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house. The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:29:34 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>EU economics chief warns France and Belgium must reduce deficit and public debt</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-eu-economics-chief-warns-france-and-belgium-must-reduce-deficit-and-public-debt</link><description>
France and Belgium must bring down their public debt and deficit levels, European Union economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis warned on Tuesday as he unveiled the European Commission's autumn economic forecast. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">065f0570-e281-11f1-84fb-2734eec1674a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:00:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg">REUTERS - Yves Herman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'A message to drug gangs': life sentences for 'barbaric' Marseille murders</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-a-message-to-drug-gangs-life-sentences-for-barbaric-marseille-murders</link><description>
Two leading figures in Marseille's drug-trafficking underworld were sentenced to life imprisonment on Monday for a triple murder in 2020. Anti-drugs activist Amine Kessaci, whose brother was among the victims, hailed the verdict as a "message to the narcocracy".

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37288fa8-dcd4-11f1-aace-7ff548d44c0a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 06:59:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner joins race for French presidency</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-olympic-judo-champion-teddy-riner-joins-race-for-french-presidency</link><description>
France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, expressing concern particularly over "the rise of the far right".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff9ac7be-dc3c-11f1-a6ee-d528d7ed3f40</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:44:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg">© AP - Michel Euler</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM's move to increase minimum wage fails to convince unions</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-pm-s-move-to-increase-minimum-wage-fails-to-convince-unions</link><description>
The French government on Monday announced a 1.6 percent increase in the national minimum wage, alongside a series of measures aimed at easing cost of living pressures. However, the decision fell well short of the demands of trade unions, who have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1fb23d3e-dc42-11f1-9f6d-714e057b766f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:36:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg">© Emma Da Silva/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'I still have nightmares': victim of police violence seeks justice six years on</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-i-still-have-nightmares-victim-of-police-violence-seeks-justice-six-years-on-michel-zecler</link><description>
Three French police officers are due to go on trial on Monday over the brutal beating of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020 – a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police violence and racism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0aa97116-dc27-11f1-890c-17b2c492ee48</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:29:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg">AFP - JOEL SAGET</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mélenchon bets on radical change as French presidential race takes shape</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-m%C3%A9lenchon-bets-on-radical-change-as-french-presidential-race-takes-shape</link><description>
Leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to pursue an uncompromising programme of radical change, as he bids for the French presidency in 2027 – despite warnings that his divisive politics could ultimately hand victory to far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">273d195c-dc1a-11f1-8d60-5f29074843e0</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:01:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg">©  KENZO TRIBOUILLARD / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French food bank donations fall as frequency of use spikes in cost of living crisis</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-drop-in-french-food-bank-collection-as-rising-cost-of-living-hits-donations</link><description>
France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living, which has left people with less to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7b3dffa-dc2b-11f1-8a7f-0f7ff0c2412a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:09:22 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg">© Mehdi Fedouach/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French MPs weigh up debate on right-wing TV channel ban as petition tops 1m</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-mps-to-weigh-debate-on-banning-conservative-tv-channel-as-petition-tops-1m-cnews</link><description>
A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to American broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received more than a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19210fc8-dc0a-11f1-bd4e-25468b64d7d5</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 06:52:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>Jack Grealish recalls a golden age of mavericks – but football has moved on</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on</link>
      <description><p>Everton forward has magical talent and popularity to burn, but has come up against hard reality of the modern game</p><p>Thomas Tuchel has never called up the player he once claimed to love “everything about”. The reason for Jack Grealish’s omission from Tuchel’s first England squad in March 2025 was given as “he simply has no rhythm”.</p><p>Catch a falling star? Grealish was suspended by Everton for three matches following “a breach of club discipline”. Suggestions his loan from Manchester City might be cancelled were calmed by David Moyes. Last week, Grealish played in a behind-closed doors friendly against Derby before issuing an Instagram statement: “I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.” Amid tabloid tales of karaoke nights and extended socialising, how close is the former boy wonder, now 31, to blowing it?</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst</link>
      <description><p>The role of full-back has changed massively in recent years. We analyse how all 20 sides are approaching the position</p><p>By <a href="https://theanalyst.com/">Opta Analyst</a></p><p>Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.</p><p>Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/biggest-leaps-across-fifa-football-rankings-the-knowledge</link>
      <description><p>Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more</p><ul><li><p><a href="mailto:knowledge@theguardian.com"><strong>Mail us</strong></a><strong> with all of your questions and answers</strong></p></li></ul><p><strong>“The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,”</strong> writes Bogdan Kotarlic. <strong>“Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?”</strong></p><p>The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings.     <item>
      <title>‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/pfa-maheta-molango-interview-fifa-gianni-infantino-interview</link>
      <description><p>At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’</p><p>After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.”</p><p>In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/pfa-maheta-molango-interview-fifa-gianni-infantino-interview">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Nations League roundup: Devenny’s divine strike lifts Northern Ireland to top tier</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/nations-league-northern-ireland-hungary-norway-denmark</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Haaland’s late penalty grabs Norway last-eight spot</p></li><li><p>Parrott penalties help Republic of Ireland secure playoff</p></li></ul><p>A wonder strike from Justin Devenny earned <strong>Northern Ireland </strong>top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the top tier of the competition. The Stoke player fired home on the volley from the edge of the area to earn a 1-1 draw away to <strong>Hungary</strong>, who would have leapfrogged Michael O’Neill’s side in the group with victory.</p><p>Northern Ireland had fallen 1-0 behind after a 35th-minute goal from the striker Barnabas Varga, who slotted home when one-on-one with the goalkeeper Pierce Charles after a defensive mix-up. The goal ended Northern Ireland’s proud record of not having conceded in this campaign and also sent Hungary to the top of the group in the live standings.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/nations-league-northern-ireland-hungary-norway-denmark">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wales-portugal-nations-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese Football Federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards.</p><p>For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia and Herzegovina – who knocked them out of World Cup qualifying this year – all potential opponents in Friday’s draw in Switzerland. Afterwards Craig Bellamy stressed the importance of keeping elite company to accelerate improvement but reiterated that he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, after which his contract expires.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wales-portugal-nations-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Former England footballer opens up on mental health</p></li><li><p>‘It was probably the lowest point’ at Manchester United</p></li></ul><p>Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai.</p><p>He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the <a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/wayne-rooney-growing-up-in-the-spotlight-fatherhood/id1527545442?i=1000802417716">Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan</a> podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wayne-rooney-contemplated-taking-own-life-during-playing-career-mental-health">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes</link>
      <description><p>A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation</p><p>“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.</p><p>The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/diego-maradona-argentina-world-cup">Argentina’s football folklore</a> are spliced with excellent archive material.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter</link>
      <description><p>In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations</p><p>I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.</p><p>As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham</link>
      <description><p>Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France </p><p>There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.</p><p>Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/nov/04/slavia-prague-arsenal-champions-league-match-report">at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days</a>, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/mar/14/arsenal-everton-premier-league-match-report">Premier League’s youngest goalscorer</a>. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/usmnt-haiti-nations-league-mauricio-pochettino</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Christian Pulisic and Julian Hall score in first half</p></li><li><p>US advance to Nations League finals 8-0 on aggregate</p></li><li><p>Mauricio Pochettino departs to take over Man United</p></li></ul><p>The US men’s national team is through to the semi-final of the Concacaf Nations League, following Saturday’s 6-0 romp with a workmanlike 2-0 win over Haiti in the Cincinnati-hosted second leg.       <title>Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland</link>
      <description><p>The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job</p><p>The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.</p><p>There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/switzerland-scotland-nations-league-match-report">4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland</a> was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary</link>
      <description><p>Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work</p><p>Danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades. Humour, enthusiasm and encyclopedic knowledge were the hallmarks of his work as a writer and editor at the New Musical Express (NME) and Q magazine, and throughout his online, TV and audio career, most prominently around his passion for football.</p><p>In 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK. He hosted radio shows on BBC 5 Live, TalkSport, BT Sport and Times Radio, as well as many podcasts including The View from the Lane, about the team he had supported since childhood, Tottenham Hotspur.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics</p><p>Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">won 3-2</a>.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-pierre-sage-sacked-steve-parish</link>
      <description><p>Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead</p><p>Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/feb/11/tottenhams-soaring-dreams-for-thomas-frank-quickly-hit-the-buffers-of-grim-reality">after being sacked by Tottenham in February</a>, but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”.</p><p>Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-pierre-sage-sacked-steve-parish">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor</link>
      <description><p>Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw</p><p>Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. <strong>Suzanne Wrack</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/chelsea-manchester-city-womens-super-league-match-report">Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor">Continue reading...</a></description>

Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Poussés par leurs succès militaires de ces derniers mois, les Houthis ne sont plus qu’à une soixantaine de kilomètres d’Aden, la ville portuaire stratégique où siège le pouvoir yéménite. La démocrate Mary Peltola a remporté, au bout du suspense, la course pour le poste de sénateur de l'Alaska, selon des résultats officiels publiés mardi. Les démocrates disposeront à partir de janvier d'une majorité de 56 sièges contre 44 à la Chambre haute, leur plus large majorité depuis 16 ans.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/90f6b112-e301-11f1-8d0c-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26308242860566.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/90f6b112-e301-11f1-8d0c-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26308242860566.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4eca4a46-e302-11f1-b328-3b31a3594493</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 03:44:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/90f6b112-e301-11f1-8d0c-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26308242860566.jpg">© Lindsey Wasson, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Asie-Pacifique</category><title>Sommet de l'Apec : Xi Jinping reçoit Vladimir Poutine avant un sommet inédit avec Donald Trump</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/asie-pacifique/20261118-sommet-de-l-apec-xi-jinping-re%C3%A7oit-vladimir-poutine-avant-un-sommet-in%C3%A9dit-avec-donald-trump</link><description>

Le Maroc n'a pas été brillant face au Niger mais la victoire (1-0) à domicile, mardi, a suffi. Assurés de participer à la CAN 2027, les Lions de l'Atlas rejoignent le Sénégal parmi les qualifiés, comme champion ou vice-champion en titre, selon la décision à venir du TAS concernant la finale de l'édition 2025.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/114f4f88-e2ce-11f1-a1aa-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/000-73KP9FD-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/114f4f88-e2ce-11f1-a1aa-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/000-73KP9FD-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5b82842-e2cd-11f1-9add-cde29bc51b04</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 22:00:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/114f4f88-e2ce-11f1-a1aa-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/000-73KP9FD-1.jpg">© Abdel Majid Bziouat, AFP</source><dc:creator>Yohann Le Coz</dc:creator></item><item><title>🔴 Israël : Matan Kahana, un fidèle d'Eisenkot, élu président du Parlement</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/moyen-orient/20261117-isra%C3%ABl-matan-kahana-un-fid%C3%A8le-d-eisenkot-%C3%A9lu-pr%C3%A9sident-du-parlement%20Isra%C3%ABl%20:%20Matan%20Kahana%2C%20un%20fid%C3%A8le%20d%27Eisenkot%2C%20%C3%A9lu%20pr%C3%A9sident%20du%20Parlement%20-%20France%2024%20Le%20centriste%20Gadi%20Eisenkot%20a%20fait%20%C3%A9lire%20Matan%20Kahana%2C%20l%27un%20des%20siens%2C%20%C3%A0%20la%20t%C3%AAte%20du%20parlement%20isra%C3%A9lien%2C%20renforcant%20son%20camp%20face%20au%20Premier%20ministre%20sortant%20Benjamin%20Netanyahu%2C%20en%20pleine%20bataille%20p...</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">50f7b1f8-e2cd-11f1-b7c8-1f7135d26f3c</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 21:24:46 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Moyen-Orient</category><title>Israël : Matan Kahana, un fidèle d'Eisenkot, élu président du Parlement</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/moyen-orient/20261117-isra%C3%ABl-matan-kahana-un-fid%C3%A8le-d-eisenkot-%C3%A9lu-pr%C3%A9sident-du-parlement</link><description>
Matan Kahana, ancien militaire proche du centriste Gadi Eisenkot, a été élu mardi à la tête du parlement israélien. Un revers pour le camp de Benjamin Netanyahu, dont l'opposition entend rapidement détricoter l'héritage législatif.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/855e62f8-e290-11f1-bec3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321467242182.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/855e62f8-e290-11f1-bec3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321467242182.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">064981e0-e2cd-11f1-997d-e7ec6ae11c25</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 21:23:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/855e62f8-e290-11f1-bec3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321467242182.jpg">© Ohad Zwigenberg</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Sports</category><title>CAN 2027: le Burkina Faso valide son billet et celui du Bénin, le Mali et le Cameroun qualifiés</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261117-can-2027-le-burkina-faso-valide-son-billet-et-celui-du-b%C3%A9nin-le-mali-et-le-cameroun-qualifi%C3%A9s-%C3%A9galement</link><description>
Pluie de qualifications à la CAN 2027 dans les matches de la soirée de ce mardi 17 novembre. Le Mali est allé gagner au Rwanda (2-0) pour décrocher son billet. Le Burkina Faso a fait de même avec une victoire 3-1 contre la Mauritanie, qui profite mathématiquement au Bénin. Les Étalons et les Écureuils sont ainsi les deux qualifiés du groupe F. Tandis que le Cameroun se qualifie sans jouer à la faveur de la victoire des Comores contre le Congo-Brazzaville (1-0).
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/14634426-e2c5-11f1-95ca-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89JT6LP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/14634426-e2c5-11f1-95ca-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89JT6LP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f7a30dda-e2c4-11f1-8791-d75b254171a9</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 20:59:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/14634426-e2c5-11f1-95ca-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89JT6LP.jpg">© Paul Ellis, AFP</source><dc:creator>Yohann Le Coz</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Que fait le Salvador en Haïti ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261117-que-fait-le-salvador-en-ha%C3%AFti</link><description>
Les Nations unies ont appelé mardi 17 novembre les forces de sécurité en Haïti à donner la priorité à la protection de la population. Plus de 2 000 soldats salvadoriens ont été déployés en Haïti fin octobre pour secourir quatre aviateurs qui faisaient partie d'une force internationale de lutte contre les gangs et qui ont disparu après une attaque près de la capitale Port-au-Prince. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b085eb8a-e2c3-11f1-9062-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/minia-HAITI-SALVADOR.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b085eb8a-e2c3-11f1-9062-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/minia-HAITI-SALVADOR.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d2425e02-e2c3-11f1-ac8f-69e4935a237d</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 20:52:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Élément Terre, la quotidienne</category><title>COP31 : un projet de déclaration finale qui fait polémique</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/%C3%A9l%C3%A9ment-terre-la-quotidienne/20261117-cop31-un-projet-de-d%C3%A9claration-finale-qui-fait-pol%C3%A9mique</link><description>
À la COP, les ministres de l'Environnement négocient la déclaration finale. Le projet de texte reprend toutes les propositions des différentes parties et se contredit parfois. Une exhaustivité contre-productive qui pourrait conduire à un échec des négociations. L'Union européenne, par la voix de son commissaire au climat, se dit prête à renoncer à la mention de l'origine décarbonnée de l'électricité dans le paragraphe sur l'électrification, dans le but de trouver un accord.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cbe23658-e2bf-11f1-be73-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-d1149adc.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cbe23658-e2bf-11f1-be73-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-d1149adc.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3f32932c-e2c1-11f1-a222-83b61e3aa622</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 19:58:23 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Audrey RACINE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Le débat</category><title>"Fractures françaises" : jusqu'où ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/le-d%C3%A9bat/20261117-fractures-fran%C3%A7aises-jusqu-o%C3%B9</link><description>
La mobilisation se poursuit en France. Les fonctionnaires ont battu le pavé dans plusieurs villes du pays pour réclamer une hausse des salaires face à l'inflation. Des lycéens et des étudiants étaient également présents dans les cortèges. Selon la CGT, quelque 500 000 personnes ont manifesté à travers la France, dont 175 000 à Paris. De son côté, le ministère de l'Intérieur estime le nombre de manifestants à 146 000, dont 28 000 dans la capitale.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a40254e-e29c-11f1-af7f-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321532844874-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a40254e-e29c-11f1-af7f-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321532844874-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5f84f766-e2b5-11f1-a336-b5aa3854af47</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 19:20:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Stéphanie ANTOINE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Journal de l'Afrique</category><title>Francophonie : face à l'impasse, l'élection du secrétaire général repoussée d'un an</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/journal-de-l-afrique/20261117-francophonie-face-%C3%A0-l-impasse-l-%C3%A9lection-du-secr%C3%A9taire-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral-repouss%C3%A9e-d-un-an</link><description>
L'élection du secrétaire général de l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), au coeur d'un bras de fer entre République démocratique du Congo et Rwanda, a été reportée d'un an lundi faute de consensus, un "compromis" diversement accueilli. La sortante rwandaise Louise Mushikiwabo, qui a dénoncé des "pressions nombreuses et fortes" à son encontre, restera en place jusqu'à la tenue du nouveau scrutin, auquel le Rwanda ne présentera pas de candidat.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1393afbe-e206-11f1-aa0f-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/DN198070-A-01-20261111.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1393afbe-e206-11f1-aa0f-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/DN198070-A-01-20261111.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">353de444-e2b6-11f1-8853-031b5c15add3</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:51:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Célia CARACENA</dc:creator></item><item><category>Sports</category><title>CAN 2027: l'Algérie s'écroule au Togo, la Tunisie ne gagne toujours pas</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261117-can-2027-l-alg%C3%A9rie-s-%C3%A9croule-au-togo-la-tunisie-ne-gagne-toujours-pas</link><description>
L'Algérie avait besoin d'une victoire pour espérer une qualification dès la 4e journée de ces éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. À la place, les Fennecs se sont complètement écroulés au Togo (3-0). La Tunisie, qui avait besoin de gagner pour se relancer et prendre confiance, a fait match nul contre la Libye, sur fond de polémique pour un penalty sifflé trop généreusement.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a790610-e2b2-11f1-bae3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2304695297.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a790610-e2b2-11f1-bae3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2304695297.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4f90fd94-e2b2-11f1-8ad8-57dac076eb8b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:24:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a790610-e2b2-11f1-bae3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2304695297.jpg">© NurPhoto via Getty Images</source><dc:creator>Yohann Le Coz</dc:creator></item><item><title>CAN 2027: la Sierra Leone retarde la qualification de la RD Congo, la Côte d'Ivoire freinée par la Gambie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261117-can-2027-la-rdc-retarde-sa-qualification-la-c%C3%B4te-d-ivoire-ralentie-en-gambie</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">fc71cbac-e2b1-11f1-9202-bf2fcc3a9b4f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:11:37 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Sports</category><title>CAN 2027 : la RD Congo retarde sa qualification, la Côte d'Ivoire ralentie en Gambie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261117-can-2027-la-rdc-retarde-sa-qualification-la-c%C3%B4te-d-ivoire-ralentie-en-gambie</link><description>
La Côte d'Ivoire et la RD Congo avaient besoin d'une victoire ce mardi 17 novembre, respectivement contre la Gambie et la Sierra Leone, pour valider leur billet pour la CAN 2027. Le travail n'a pas été fait. Les Léopards ont concédé le nul en toute fin de match (1-1). Les Éléphants, eux, se sont fait surprendre par les Gambiens après avoir mené au score (2-2) et voient le suspense relancé dans leur groupe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d06fdf96-e2af-11f1-b843-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B4X276N.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d06fdf96-e2af-11f1-b843-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B4X276N.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33dff87e-e2a9-11f1-868d-4937d01672fb</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:08:16 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d06fdf96-e2af-11f1-b843-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B4X276N.jpg">© Nicolas Tucat, AFP</source><dc:creator>Yohann Le Coz</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Comment une fausse citation de Christine Lagarde a été amplifiée par un réseau de désinformation srilankais</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261117-comment-fausse-citation-christine-lagarde-amplifi%C3%A9e-par-r%C3%A9seau-d%C3%A9sinformation-sri-lanka</link><description>
Selon plusieurs publications Facebook, Christine Lagarde aurait déclaré que "les personnes âgées vivent trop longtemps", ce qui représenterait un "risque" pour l’économie. Une fausse citation attribuée à tort à la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne, actuellement relayée par un réseau de désinformation basé au Sri Lanka.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ee6d5e26-e2a8-11f1-b668-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/image2-154.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ee6d5e26-e2a8-11f1-b668-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/image2-154.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1995705c-e2a9-11f1-ae40-7f6b8fd6a643</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:31:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ee6d5e26-e2a8-11f1-b668-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/image2-154.png">© X</source><dc:creator>Les Observateurs</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>L'actualité économique et politique en Europe - RFI</title><description>Suivez l'actualité en direct dédiée au continent Européen - Les derniers reportages, news et informations en continu en Europe, Emissions, Podcast, dossiers sur RFI.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 06:58:13 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine: en Crimée ou à Kiev, les frappes contre des ponts perturbent la logistique et le quotidien</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261118-guerre-en-ukraine-en-crim%C3%A9e-ou-%C3%A0-kiev-les-frappes-contre-des-ponts-perturbent-la-logistique-et-le-quotidien</link><description>
En début de semaine, la Russie et l'Ukraine ont à nouveau multiplié les frappes. L'Ukraine a frappé le pont de Kertch, en Crimée, causant d'importants dégâts à cette infrastructure importante pour le ravitaillement russe. De son côté, la Russie a mené plusieurs attaques contre des ponts à Kiev, rendant ainsi la vie difficile dans la capitale ukrainienne.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/94298844-e312-11f1-acd6-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321401562180.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/94298844-e312-11f1-acd6-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321401562180.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c9b65388-e313-11f1-a76c-1fbd63ebc9be</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 06:08:19 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/94298844-e312-11f1-acd6-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321401562180.jpg">© Evgeniy Maloletka / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Allemagne: la Deutsche Bank au cœur d'un nouveau scandale de pratiques douteuses</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-allemagne-la-deutsche-bank-au-c%C5%93ur-d-un-nouveau-scandale-de-pratiques-douteuses</link><description>
La plus grande institution bancaire allemande fait une nouvelle fois la une de la presse, mardi 17 novembre 2026. Une fuite de 15 millions de documents lève le voile sur ses pratiques douteuses et la manière dont la Deutsche Bank a protégé ses clients les plus sulfureux, comme le pédocriminel américain Jeffrey Epstein.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d113dcd2-e2a4-11f1-9635-7d42f883cc1b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:35:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bf6972a8-e2a4-11f1-8961-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/ALLEMAGNE-BERLIN-DEUTSCHE-BANK.jpg">REUTERS - Nadja Wohlleben</source><dc:creator>Nathanaël Vittrant</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Projet de «hub de retour»: «On n'a aucune idée de la manière dont le Rwanda va traiter ces étrangers»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261117-projet-de-hub-de-retour-on-n-a-aucune-id%C3%A9e-de-la-mani%C3%A8re-dont-le-rwanda-va-traiter-ces-%C3%A9trangers</link><description>
« Ni avenir, ni humanité dans le projet de centre de migrants au Rwanda » : ce sont les mots du Premier ministre espagnol, Pedro Sanchez, face à l'initiative détaillée, lundi 16 novembre, par cinq pays de l'Union européenne, dont l'Allemagne et le Danemark, d'ouvrir dans ce pays le tout premier centre pour des migrants expulsés d'Europe. Les promoteurs du projet assurent vouloir créer un centre ouvert, où les migrants seront accompagnés et pourront bénéficier de programmes de formation, d'accès à l’emploi, ainsi qu'à l'éducation et à des centres de santé. Assiste-t-on à un tournant dans le durcissement de l'Europe en matière d'immigration ? L'analyse d'Antoine Pecoud, professeur de sociologie à l'université de Sorbonne Paris-Nord et directeur du département Policy de l'Institut des migrations. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f886fa4-a8eb-11f1-80af-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-04T160250Z-834668253-RC2CCNAR7GC0-RTRMADP-3-EU-IMMIGRATION.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f886fa4-a8eb-11f1-80af-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-04T160250Z-834668253-RC2CCNAR7GC0-RTRMADP-3-EU-IMMIGRATION.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">21af5d90-e27f-11f1-8e59-9ff547092806</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:02:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Comment l’Ukraine a en partie détruit le pont de Kertch en Crimée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-comment-l-ukraine-a-en-partie-d%C3%A9truit-le-pont-de-kertch</link><description>
Cible prioritaire de l’Ukraine depuis le début de l’invasion russe, le pont de Kertch reliant la Crimée à la Russie n’est plus utilisable. Après de premières frappes lundi 16 novembre, l’armée ukrainienne a de nouveau ciblé cet ouvrage à la fois stratégique et symbolique ce mardi. Les images disponibles en sources ouvertes montrent qu’une partie importante de la section routière a été détruite.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efa87d34-e285-11f1-8673-6541d1e7a339</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:11:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6de17860-e284-11f1-adba-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/Russie-Ukraine-Kertch-Info-Verif-Une.png">© Captures d'écran/ Montage RFI</source><dc:creator>Grégory Genevrier</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>«C'est un jour historique»: en Serbie, le mouvement des étudiants fait son entrée au Parlement</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-c-est-un-jour-historique-en-serbie-le-mouvement-des-%C3%A9tudiants-fait-son-entr%C3%A9e-au-parlement</link><description>
Ce mardi 17 novembre marque la première session du Parlement nouvellement élu en Serbie, qui consacre la victoire de la liste étudiante après deux ans de manifestations anticorruption.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c2f50a0-e279-11f1-97b9-0be1f30c0e1f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:33:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/73fb2964-e278-11f1-a3a1-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T092505Z-1014948375-RC2LPOAZ0JM3-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg">© Zorana Jevtic / Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Soldats français déployés en Ukraine: Moscou y voit une «participation directe» au conflit</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-d%C3%A9ploy%C3%A9s-en-ukraine-moscou-y-voit-une-participation-directe-au-conflit</link><description>
Ce mardi 17 novembre, le ministre russe des Affaires étrangères a qualifié de « participation directe » au conflit en Ukraine le déploiement de soldats français opérant en Ukraine pour des missions de formation et d'entretien de matériels, révélé lundi par RFI.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cc8b09f6-e277-11f1-9c03-0f08de7ca9eb</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:14:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5112e664-3a74-11f1-904f-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26062382346034.jpg">© Pavel Bednyakov/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : que cache la mission secrète des militaires français?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261117-guerre-en-ukraine-que-cache-la-mission-secr%C3%A8te-des-militaires-fran%C3%A7ais</link><description>
C’est une information RFI : des soldats français sont présents en Ukraine depuis l’été dernier. Selon notre enquête, ils sont réunis au sein d’un dispositif confidentiel baptisé « Volia ». Leur mission : former des militaires ukrainiens pour assurer la maintenance des équipements livrés par Paris, notamment les canons Caesar et les avions Mirage 2000. Ils ne prennent pas part aux combats. La France n’a toutefois pas confirmé officiellement l’existence de cette mission. Pourquoi cette opération n’a-t-elle pas été portée à la connaissance du Parlement ? Et comment la Russie peut-elle interpréter cette présence militaire française sur le sol ukrainien ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1ef1b610-e01e-11f1-9b8c-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-Par8194826.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6edbc838-e1ad-11f1-9213-e1d07338c648</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:00:19 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item><item><category>Appels sur l'actualité</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : 400 000 Russes morts sur le front?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/appels-sur-l-actualit%C3%A9/20261117-guerre-en-ukraine-400-000-russes-morts-sur-le-front</link><description>
Près de 400 000 soldats russes auraient péri depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine. C’est ce que révèlent des documents attribués à l’institut de statistiques russe Rosstat, dont deux groupes de hackers affirment avoir piraté les données. Des révélations particulièrement sensibles, alors que Vladimir Poutine a classé les informations sur les pertes militaires au secret d’État dès 2015. Comment ces hackers ont-ils pu accéder à ces données ? Ces chiffres sont-ils vraiment crédibles ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12463d34-9854-11ed-bc0b-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/AP23003562030298.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12463d34-9854-11ed-bc0b-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/AP23003562030298.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1e6ce9c6-e1ae-11f1-823e-1b46fca9b9c5</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:56:28 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juan Gomez</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Nouvel échange de frappes entre la Russie et l'Ukraine, deux morts en Crimée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261117-la-russie-frappe-deux-ponts-majeurs-%C3%A0-kiev-l-ukraine-cible-%C3%A0-nouveau-la-crim%C3%A9e</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">95f153a6-e253-11f1-b160-a15f137c0baa</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 06:54:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/63468264-e253-11f1-9b57-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7KG3CQ.jpg">AFP - STRINGER</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Accents d'Europe</category><title>Sur les traces des personnes réduites en esclavage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/accents-d-europe/20261116-sur-les-traces-des-personnes-r%C3%A9duites-en-esclavage</link><description>
Donner un nom, une histoire, à des millions d’asservis et comprendre l’impact de la traite sur les inégalités d’aujourd’hui : dans cette émission, on ouvre les registres britanniques de l’esclavage.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7ccb2-02c6-11ed-b799-005056bfa79e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17198587355318.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7ccb2-02c6-11ed-b799-005056bfa79e/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17198587355318.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d9124e66-e1f8-11f1-bfcd-390d5e1d14eb</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 21:20:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Juliette Gheerbrant</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Espagne: Lula da Silva soutient Pedro Sanchez avant les législatives anticipées du 29 novembre</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-espagne-lula-da-silva-soutient-pedro-sanchez-avant-les-l%C3%A9gislatives-anticip%C3%A9es-du-29-novembre</link><description>
Le Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sanchez a reçu, lundi 16 novembre, le soutien du président brésilien Lula da Silva à Madrid, à moins de deux semaines des élections législatives anticipées du 29 novembre. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ac6cf11e-e1e8-11f1-bb05-5d0ba7174a9f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:53:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/6c241fe8-e1e7-11f1-90be-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320393432966.jpg">© AP Photo/Francisco Seco</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Soldats français en Ukraine: «Cela va sans doute amplifier la réaction de propagande de la Russie»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-en-ukraine-cela-va-sans-doute-amplifier-la-r%C3%A9action-de-propagande-de-la-russie</link><description>

Cinq pays européens défendent une politique migratoire très ferme et pilotent ensemble un projet visant à envoyer des migrants dans des centres situés hors d’Europe. Après des mois de réflexion, ils ont retenu le Rwanda pour un premier projet pilote, dont l’ouverture est prévue en 2027.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bff09a3a-e1d2-11f1-86ed-abe06ccee855</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:35:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/013e2372-e1d3-11f1-80e8-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26320558302536.jpg">AP Photo/Heinz-Peter Bader - Heinz-Peter Bader</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Soldats français en Ukraine: «Nous ne sommes pas cobelligérants», rappelle le sénateur PS Rachid Temal</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261116-soldats-fran%C3%A7ais-en-ukraine-nous-ne-sommes-pas-cobellig%C3%A9rants-rappelle-le-s%C3%A9nateur-ps-rachid-temal</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/dd94df9c-ae02-11f0-a21b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/Ukraine-Soldats-Armee-Russie-Guerre.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/dd94df9c-ae02-11f0-a21b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/Ukraine-Soldats-Armee-Russie-Guerre.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dc79170e-e1c8-11f1-9f22-1b5d0dc6ca69</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:03:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Belgique: le roi Philippe accorde une semaine de plus à Bart De Wever pour boucler le budget</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261116-belgique-le-roi-philippe-accorde-une-semaine-de-plus-%C3%A0-bart-de-wever-pour-boucler-le-budget</link><description>
Le Premier ministre belge a dû partager le constat que les négociations sur le budget n'aboutissent toujours pas au sein de sa coalition.
